draft.title: Rates of change in context
card: The derivative dV/dt is the rate of change of V with respect to time t. Its units are the units of V per unit of t, such as litres per minute.
To find how fast a quantity changes at a given moment, write it as a function of t, differentiate, then substitute that value of t.
A positive rate means the quantity is increasing. A negative rate means it is decreasing.
Example: water in a tank is V = 40t − t² litres after t minutes. Then dV/dt = 40 − 2t. At t = 5, dV/dt = 40 − 10 = 30, so the volume is rising at 30 litres per minute.
draft.remember: Differentiate, then substitute the time. The sign of the answer shows whether the quantity is rising or falling.

a.q: The water in a tank is V = 60t − t² litres after t minutes. How fast is the volume changing at t = 10?
a.why: dV/dt = 60 − 2t, so at t = 10 the rate is 60 − 20 = 40. It is positive, so the volume is increasing. The value 500 is V itself, found by substituting without differentiating.
a.clue: Differentiate first, then put in t = 10.

b.q: The water in a pool is V = 200 + 12t − 3t² litres after t minutes. What is the rate of change of volume at t = 4?
b.why: dV/dt = 12 − 6t, so at t = 4 the rate is 12 − 24 = −12. The negative sign means the volume is decreasing. Choosing increasing at 12 ignores the sign.
b.clue: Check the sign of your answer.
